steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: You really sure about leaving the village?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I'll be off at first light tomorrow.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The fields have already been replowed, there's plenty of seeds and grain, and the storehouse has also been fixed. As for the ferrying, I've taught a few of the young ones. Don't worry.

steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: I'm worried about you, Xanthos.

steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: You've never left the marsh before, and now you want to run off into the distance, all to find a stranger?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Ithakos is my brother. He's helped us all out before.

steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: It's been an entire year. Maybe he's already headed back to Athenius... That's where he was from, it makes sense.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The things he agreed to do, he will do.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Once the war is over, he will return. He promised me.

steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: Have you ever considered... if... if he's already...

steps.name: Concerned Villager
steps.text: He went off... to fight the Sargonians...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Then I shall avenge him. I shall avenge the Minoans.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: Hey, don't get so worked up! You've got the wrong guy! I'm really not your Ithakos or whatever it was!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The one getting worked up is you, friend. I merely recognized the armor you wear.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It belonged to Ithakos, my brother. Before he left, every family in our village donated leather and iron for it. I was the one who made that set of armor presentable, and forged him his weapon.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: F-Forgive me, I've been battling for so long now, big battles, small ones, and it's been a long time since I had some proper sleep. My mind's...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Here. There's still some calming herbal tea in the pot.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Can you tell me who you got this armor from?

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: Another guerrilla friend. We ran into a skirmish... He took an arrow, and before he died, he gave it to me...

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: But his name wasn't Ithakos.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: You see all these marks on the armor? It must've passed through a lot of hands to get that many...

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: You might not know this, but we guerrillas aren't like the Sargonian army. We're not well-supplied.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: Everyone gathers up weapons, armor and food, which get given out depending on the mission's priority.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: I can tell you that fallen guerrilla's unit number, and that'll get you where you need to be. Oh, right, let me give you the armor back first.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Keep it. It's still of use to you. Just telling me the way is enough, friend.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: If you insist, but are you sure you want to search the mountains?

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: These mountains are our stomping grounds, and where we battle the Sargonians...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Then I'll join you.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member A
steps.text: You ever seen a battlefield before?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: (Shakes head) Before all this, I had only ever held oars and farm tools.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: But we have no other choice, do we?

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: Sorry, I don't really remember the smiling, long-haired Forte you mentioned.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: As for these boots, I got given them when I joined the guerrillas... According to the friend who gave them to me, they belonged to a middle-aged guy who was missing a chunk out of his left horn.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: There's a hole in them.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: S-Sorry. They're a little small for me, and I haven't had the time to mend them.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: Those Sargonians have been chasing us this entire time. If you hadn't shown up to support us in the nick of time...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Sit down.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I'll help you mend them.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member B
steps.text: Na'sai kala... Wow, you've got big hands, but they're nimble... How long've you been one of us?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Four months. I came here to find someone, at first.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Keep the boots.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Fighting, marching, hiding, reorganizing. You bleed, you die, or you wipe your sword, then you jump into the next battle... Days like these are long ones.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Where's the man who gave you these boots? Just point me the way, friend.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: I knew this letter carved on the corner of this shield meant something... You're saying it's short for 'Ithakos', and you carved it?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: So you've spent half a year wandering the battlefields, staying with pretty much every one of our bands, just to find this guy?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It seems you don't have much you can tell me either.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: Sorry, Xanthos. Also, I don't plan on giving this shield back to you.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: Look at just how many blade marks there are on it! And these black marks... Sargonian Arts can barely make a dent in it!

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: I need to keep it. It'll let me protect more of our friends, maybe even keep me alive long enough to go home one day.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: If that is the case, then I couldn't be happier.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Let the name 'Ithakos' stay by your side. Let our blood, our eyes, be witness to our victory.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member C
steps.text: This is where we part, my friend.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Just point me the way. It is all I ask.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Try changing hands. Ithakos was left-handed, which I kept in mind when I made this Arts unit for him.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: I knew it! I knew something felt off about the power levels!

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: ...It's already been a whole year, Xanthos.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Time flies, as swift as a melted river.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: You're already the most famous guerrilla in the mountains. You've fought the most fights, walked the most battlefields. Everybody sings of your heroism...

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: Are you really going to keep searching for your brother?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I have no reason to stop.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Like how you will not turn and leave the battlefield.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: Hah, you're right.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Your accent. You're from Lachedamon?

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: I sure am. Well, more specifically, my hometown is on the route the nomadic city follows. It's a river valley, absolutely beautiful in spring.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I've just told you about my hometown, the village Ithakos and I founded together. You should tell me more about yours.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: We have been losing this war for over a hundred years. We do not know how it will end. We should remember each other's hometowns... We should remember each other.

steps.name: Guerrilla Squad Member D
steps.text: I'll be more than happy to, my friend.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I continue my search tomorrow. Just point me the way, friend.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: Why must I suffer the indignity of being tied to this tree, Minoan?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Like I said, answer my question.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: Ithakos, Ithakos, Ithakos! Always about Ithakos!

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: Fine, fine, tozz feek, I've had enough... Two years ago, my troops met with Minoan guerrillas near here. They were escorting some wounded.

spans.text: I've had enough... Two years ago, my troops met with Minoan guerrillas near here. They were escorting some wounded.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: I remember their ensign, matches the unit you mentioned.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: We wiped them out. That Ithakos you keep talking about should've been one of them.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: You happy now? Did you seriously set up an ambush for the sake of a battle two years ago, so you could capture me and have your revenge?

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: You're mad, Minoan, an absolute lunatic!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You might not believe me, but this is all just a coincidence.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Before today, I was not thinking of finding Ithakos, or killing his enemies.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: This battle is no different to the ones of the past year, no, the past century.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You invaded land that doesn't belong to you, Sargonian, and we have no choice but to defend our home.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I have simply become accustomed to asking everyone I meet: 'Have you seen Ithakos? Have you seen that smiling, long-haired Forte? He's from Athenius, but he has a south country accent.'

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Such a thing truly does mean I am, as you say, 'mad'.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I have found his armor, his boots, his shield, his Arts unit... Everything he left behind on this wooded mountain, I have found.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I have found him.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I have never once thought you invaders would remember the name of every Minoan you met. Your padishahs hardly care about what every line in your books of merit actually means, do they?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: That said... Ithakos. Remember this name.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It is our passion, our love, and your crime, your punishment.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Now, tell me.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Where was that battle, exactly?!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Which of these firs was watered with the blood of Minos?!

a.text: Xanthos looks up, and sees countless Minoan firs, standing tall. The wind blows, and the entire forest rustles.
This land, these woods. They remember many things, but they do not speak.
His brother, his friend, the youth who followed his revelation and left home. He died here, somewhere. Everywhere.
Ithakos, countless Ithakoses, have left not even bones, all for the sake of the land beneath their feet.
Xanthos lifts the giant oar in his hand. After an entire year, it has forgotten the river's burble. Now, all that can wet it is the blood of his enemy!

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Did you avenge Ithakos?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Just as I was about to smash in the head of that Sargonian with my weapon, my friend stopped me, while the bugles cried out.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: You never told me the campaign you experienced was...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The final battle before Minos and Sargon signed a ceasefire. Minos, which had lost for a hundred years,

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: hah, had finally won.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: That friend of mine desperately held back my hand. He had a broken leg, yet he could still bring such strength to bear to rein me in.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I turned, and saw his face full of tears, and his eyes full of fear... Not towards the Sargonians, but towards me.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I knew what he was so afraid of.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: He was afraid I would destroy this hard-won 'peace'. He was afraid I would bring about new conflict, that I would extend this cruel war. He was afraid he would become like Ithakos, forever unable to return home.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: My pent-up rage and grief had nowhere to go. All I could do was watch that Sargonian officer kneel on the ground, numbly listening to the bugles. The same numbness I felt...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It was that moment I knew the war will rage on in our bodies. It had begun, and it could never end.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You are right. The Minos in my heart no longer exists. It died on the battlefield many years ago, alongside the Ithakoses.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: But I will not allow the enemy to defile our land again. Not even if they had built this city.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: 'Not even if they had built this city'... So, even the textbooks say that nowadays?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Ithakos went to your village, so full of passion, unlike me. He must have taught you many building techniques.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Indeed. He renovated nearly every important building in the village.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: His techniques were passed down from his ancestors. During the occupation, my own grandfather was pressed into service by the Sargonians to build the nomadic cities, thanks to his mastery of engineering.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: The mobility layer of this Athenius might just be his handiwork.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Forgive me, I was far too rude to you earlier. I...

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Do not bow your head for that, boy.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: I am not the engineer who built the nomadic cities, I don't have proof of how much our ancestors toiled building Athenius. All that data was taken away by the Sargonians.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: The Sargonians wanted the Minoan engineers' data... but why?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: An engineer's notes will always have something more than just jargon and modification blueprints.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: He had to keep track of the quantities of building materials, while coordinating transport and construction teams, so he was a meticulous planner of manpower, and remembered the names of every worker.

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: Not Sargonian workers, but the names of those from Minos, and where they came from, and how the Sargonians forced them to do their bidding.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Minoan workers? As I recall, current mainstream thinking is that Padishah Malla did not use any Minoan workers for heavy labor while the Three Poleis were being built.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Do you mean to say...?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: History was not written by us, not even our final victory.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: But there is evidence of wrongdoing, evidence that should be shared with the public. Do you remember where these engineer's notes are?

steps.name: Ithakos's Father
steps.text: How should I know? Ask the Sargonians... Ah, but those Sargonians are probably dead by now, haha...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Ask the Sargonians... The construction of the Three Poleis...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: What is it, Master?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The Sargonian mission is not using the exchange to obtain technical data, but rather, the notes detailing proof of the Sargonians' sins!
